To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a collaborative approach to backup in the mobile environment requires the implementation of a distributed storage system that can handle a variety of constraints and that the performance of the system is highly dependent on the compression algorithm used.

1) a collaborative backup system must provide the following storage services: (a) storage of the user’s data, (b) storage of the backup data, and (c) storage of the metadata, 2) the backup data should be compressed, 3) the metadata should be stored in the user’s device and in the server, and 4) the backup data can be compressed in the user’s or the server’s device.

the design and implementation of the storage subsystem of a mobile collaborative backup system should be based on a tradeoff between the cost of storage and the performance of backup and restore operations, that a compression method that is both fast and effective can be implemented in a collaborative system, and that the use of a collaborative system can be a cost-effective way to implement a mobile backup service.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a collaborative backup service for mobile devices.
the design of storage systems that can be deployed in a wide range of environments, from mobile devices to the cloud.
the design and implementation of a fault-tolerant collaborative backup service that exploits spontaneous interactions between mobile devices.

the paper is a very good contribution to the area of fault tolerance in mobile devices and the authors are to be commended for the effort they have put into it.
the paper is a good example of how to analyze the storage layer in a collaborative backup service for mobile devices and how to implement it in a prototype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is important to understand the constraints of the mobile environment, and to take them into account when designing and implementing a backup service.
the storage system is the most important component in a collaborative backup service for mobile devices and that it should be designed with the mobile environment in mind.
we have designed and implemented an efficient and scalable storage system for a mobile collaborative backup system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the storage layer of a collaborative backup service for mobile devices should not only provide fault-tolerance, but also minimize the storage and bandwidth costs.

the mobile environment poses unique challenges to the design and implementation of a collaborative backup service and that these challenges are not limited to the networking layer but extend to storage.
the design of a backup service for mobile devices requires careful attention to the tradeoffs between the storage requirements and the performance and reliability of the system.
